prompt:
A wide 4:1 landscape picture, a side-view effect, the stun loop that circles above the Keeper, a clockwork owl, for a 2D game, painted as four animation stages of one effect that float side by side on open, empty green. Only the effect is painted; whatever it touches or comes from stays off the canvas. The four stages share one horizontal centre line, centred at one sixteenth, three sixteenths, five sixteenths and so on up to fifteen sixteenths of the picture width, with the same wide band of empty green around each, so every stage sits alone in the open and none comes near another or the picture edge. Everything is drawn in flat side view with no perspective, at the size of a game sprite; the longest stage spans about a fifth of the picture width.

Branching blue-white electric arcs crackle in the air above the owl's shoulder: a loose tangle of three or four jagged forked bolts, each with a hot ivory-white core and a cool pale-blue #8EC9F0 glow that stays close to the bolt, with small bright sparks at the fork tips. Between the bolts hang a few broken pieces of cracked clock-face brass, #94611E, as angular shards. The four stages are four phases of one crackle: in each, the bolts fork and jump to different angles while the overall tangle keeps the same size and centre. The palette is ivory #FFF5DC and pale blue #8EC9F0 for the arcs, deep bronze #94611E and dark iron grey-brown #3A3328 for the shards, with a near-black ink edge. Shapes are angular, like cracks in glass.

Eight distinct frames, not four: each of the stages described above is shown as two consecutive steps, the second slightly further along than the first, so no two of the eight frames are alike and the motion reads smoothly from left to right. Draw big and bold: every shape is large, filling most of the height of the picture, with a thick, bold near-black ink outline (about a twelfth of the shape's width), strong contrast from near-black shadow to bright cream highlights, visible etched cross-hatching on the shaded sides, and a clear angular forked design with small ink-edged shards and sparks around it. Shapes read clearly even when shrunk to a tiny game sprite.

Style: a dark painterly etched storybook illustration, ink and wash with fine etched cross-hatching and a faint paper grain inside the shapes only. Large shapes have a clean near-black ink outline #171614 about 2 px wide at this size; hair-thin streaks and tiny sparks carry a hairline ink edge so they keep their colour. One light source sits in front and slightly above: upper edges brighter, lower edges shaded with fine hatching. The glow stays inside each shape, brightest at the core and fading toward the ink outline. The background is one perfectly flat, even, pure green #00FF00 from edge to edge, the shapes cut cleanly against it, and the shapes themselves use only the palette above. The canvas holds only the eight effects floating on the green, as a clean sprite strip with nothing else on it.

Style (required): dark, muted ink on aged paper, like an etched storybook engraving. Etched ink linework with near-black ink outlines; crosshatch and fine line hatching for every shadow and form; visible aged paper grain and fibre texture under all colour; hand-printed, slightly uneven ink. No flat fills, no vector shapes, no smooth digital gradients, no glossy 3D rendering.
